meeting_notes.title: First meeting
meeting_notes.text:
First meeting with Jane Fraser, 13 October 2026. Attendees: Jane Fraser, Isabel (RM).

Isabel: Thank you for coming in, Jane. Let's start with you. Could you tell me about your background and how you earn your income?
Jane: I am the Chief Executive Officer of CityBank. I was born on 14 March 1981, so I am 45 now. My pay is a salary plus a performance bonus, and together that comes to an annual income of S$10m. I do not have a business of my own or any rental income, so it all comes from my job.
Isabel: And the assets you would like us to manage?
Jane: Investable assets managed with the bank total S$500m.

Isabel: How would you describe the way you like to invest?
Jane: Very conservatively. I have been investing mainly in deposits and bonds for years and I am not familiar with complex products. I prefer cash, government bonds and high-grade bonds, and I like to hold things for a long time rather than trade. I would like to own a small amount of blue-chip equities, up to about 10% of my assets. I believe in large, established companies with strong balance sheets and a record of paying dividends, such as banks, healthcare, utilities and consumer staples. I stay away from speculative technology, crypto and anything that needs leverage.
Isabel: Any products or sectors you want kept out of the portfolio?
Jane: I do not want hedge funds or private markets in the portfolio. I would also like to avoid tobacco and thermal coal. I have a general interest in responsible investing and I would like the portfolio to reflect that. I cannot hold shares in CityBank either, because of my position.

Isabel: What do you want the portfolio to achieve?
Jane: Keeping my capital safe comes first and steady income is second. After that I would like my assets to grow, but only modestly and without an aggressive approach. I want low risk, but steady growth. My target is for the portfolio to reach 700M within 8 years. I would not need to touch most of the capital for at least ten years, so I am a long-term investor.
Isabel: From S$500m to 700M is about 40% in total, or roughly 4.3% a year if it compounds. I will test that against what a low-risk mix can deliver.
Jane: That is fine. It is a target and not a promise, and I would rather miss it than take on a lot more risk.

Isabel: How would you feel if the portfolio fell in a bad year?
Jane: I am very risk averse. A fall of more than 10% in a single year would make me very uncomfortable and would likely prompt me to sell.

Isabel: On currencies?
Jane: Mainly SGD, with some USD.

Summary by Isabel: Jane is the Chief Executive Officer of CityBank and earns an annual income of S$10m from salary and bonus. Investable assets managed with the bank total S$500m. She is currently 45 years old, and wants her investment portfolio to hit 700M within 8 years. Her priorities are keeping her capital safe and steady income. She would like low risk but steady growth, and she will not accept an aggressive approach.

Open question: she did not state her monthly spending. Isabel will ask, run the risk questionnaire, and then send the IPS draft to the Portfolio Manager.

meeting_notes.title: Risk questionnaire follow-up
meeting_notes.text:
Follow-up meeting with Jane Fraser, 20 October 2026. Attendees: Jane Fraser, Isabel (RM).

We went through the risk questionnaire together.

Isabel: Last week you said a fall of more than 10% in a year would be hard for you. Does that still hold?
Jane: Yes. I am very risk averse. A fall of more than 10% in a single year would make me very uncomfortable and would likely prompt me to sell.
Isabel: Has that happened before?
Jane: When bond prices dropped in 2022 I kept my positions, but I worried about it daily and asked my previous adviser twice to move to cash. That is how I know my limit.
Isabel: So your willingness to take risk is low. In terms of your ability, you have a long horizon, an income of S$10m that covers your costs, and a large asset base, so you could afford more risk than you want to take. I suggest we follow your comfort level, and not your capacity.
Jane: Agreed. Please follow my comfort level.

Isabel: Let's talk about cash needs. What do you spend each month?
Jane: I spend about S$150,000 a month on living costs, and my salary covers it. I take no regular withdrawals from the portfolio. I would like to keep a cash reserve of S$30m so that I never have to sell investments to meet my expenses, whether that is an emergency or a large one-off bill in a year when markets are down.
Isabel: Anything planned over the next few years?
Jane: There is no big purchase planned. If something comes up I will tell you at least three months ahead so that we can raise the cash from the reserve.

Isabel: And taxes?
Jane: I am a Singapore tax resident and I am in the top income tax bracket of 24% on my salary and bonus. There is no tax on capital gains here, so I do not need tax-loss harvesting and I do not want the portfolio traded just for tax reasons. I would rather have low turnover. Please keep interest and dividend income simple and tell me about any foreign withholding tax.

Isabel: Is there a view on equities now?
Jane: I am now open to adding up to 15% in blue-chip equities, up from the 10% discussed at the first meeting, as the modest growth part of my assets. I prefer the rest to stay in cash, government bonds and high-grade bonds.
Isabel: And the sustainable investing point?
Jane: Please apply it as a rule, not just a nice-to-have. No tobacco and no thermal coal, and I would prefer funds that use ESG screening. I want to leave something for my family and perhaps support education charities later, but that is a distant third behind safety and income.

Isabel: Currencies?
Jane: I would like to keep my currency mix mainly in SGD, with up to 20% in USD. I would like my assets to grow steadily towards the 700M target within 8 years and I expect to stay invested for at least ten years.

Isabel: Are there any milestones coming up that we should plan around?
Jane: My daughter starts university overseas in September 2029. I plan to buy a holiday home in Phuket in 2028. I intend to retire from CityBank in 2041, when I turn 60.

Open question: she has not yet told us about assets held outside the bank or any liabilities. Isabel will ask and then update the IPS draft with the Portfolio Manager.

meeting_notes.title: Review meeting
meeting_notes.text: Marcus Lim reviewed his portfolio with his relationship manager. He is comfortable with a balanced approach and wants to keep about 20% in cash. He asked to revisit his property exposure next quarter.
